title: 고난도 · 비교/변화 (14~15번)
intro: OPIc 14~15번은 '과거와 현재 비교', '사회적 변화', '장단점과 의견'을 묻는 고난도 문제로, IH·AL을 가르는 구간입니다. 거창한 사회 분석 대신 '서울에서 혼자 사는 IT 회사 마케팅팀 직장인'인 내 경험을 근거로 쓰면 쉬운 말로도 설득력이 생깁니다. 대전에서 가족과 살던 오래된 아파트 vs 지금 혼자 사는 아파트, 금요일 재택근무, 넷플릭스 영화 밤, 출퇴근 음악, 오사카 여행 같은 이야기를 근거로 재활용하세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장('Oh, that's a really interesting question.') → 입장 또는 전체 변화 한 줄 → 이유·차이 2개 → 내 경험 예시(대전 본가, 재택근무, 오사카 여행 등) → 결론·마무리 문장('So yeah, that's what I think about ~.')
비교 문제는 In the past / used to ~ ↔ These days / Now ~ 를 짝지어 최소 2가지 차이를 말하세요.
의견 문제는 First of all / On top of that 으로 이유 2개를 확실히 나누고, 'For example, in my case ~' 로 내 경험을 꼭 넣으세요.
AL을 노린다면 장점만 말하지 말고 'That said, ~ / On the other hand, ~' 로 반대 측면을 한 번 짚은 뒤 결론을 내리세요.

expressions.en: Oh, that's a really interesting question.
In the past, people used to ~.
I think it's a good change.

expressions.note: 내 경험 예시로 넘어가는 연결 문장

expressions.en: It's much more convenient than before.
I'd say the biggest difference is ~.
expressions.ko: 가장 큰 차이는 ~라고 할 수 있어요.

expressions.en: Compared to when I was growing up, ~.
That's a big part of the reason why ~.
So yeah, that's what I think about ~.

expressions.note: 장점과 단점이 공존하는 변화를 말할 때

expressions.en: At the end of the day, it comes down to ~.
expressions.note: 결론을 정리할 때 쓰는 관용 표현

questions.en: How has housing in Korea changed over the last 20 years? What are the biggest differences between homes today and homes 20 years ago?
questions.ko: 지난 20년 동안 한국의 주거 형태는 어떻게 변했나요? 오늘날의 집과 20년 전의 집의 가장 큰 차이점은 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a really interesting question.' → 전체 변화 한 줄 → 차이 2개(1인 가구 증가로 작은 집, 디지털 도어락 같은 편의 시설 / 집값 상승) → 내 예시(대전의 오래된 아파트 vs 지금 혼자 사는 7층 아파트) → 'So yeah, ~.'
In the past, families used to ~ / These days, more and more people live alone 처럼 과거·현재를 짝지어 말하세요.
AL은 '편리해졌지만 젊은 사람이 집을 사기는 훨씬 어려워졌다'는 양면을 짚고 결론을 내리세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a really interesting question. Housing in Korea has changed a lot. In the past, big families used to live together in one home. These days, a lot of young people live alone, like me. I live alone in a small apartment in Seoul. Homes today are also more modern. My apartment has a digital door lock and a smart air conditioner. But houses are much more expensive now. Yeah, that's how housing has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think housing in Korea has changed a lot in the last 20 years. I'd say the biggest difference is the size of households. In the past, families with three generations used to live together. These days, more and more people live alone, so there are many small apartments for one person. I'm a good example. I grew up with my family in an old apartment in Daejeon, but now I live alone in a one-bedroom apartment near my office in Seoul. Another big difference is technology. My parents' old apartment had a key and a noisy heater, but my place has a digital door lock and everything is controlled by an app. On the other hand, homes are much more expensive now. So yeah, that's how housing has changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I'd say housing in Korea has changed dramatically over the last 20 years, and I can see it in my own life. The biggest difference is probably the size of households. Back in the day, it was really common for grandparents, parents and kids to live together under one roof. These days, though, more and more people live on their own, so you see tons of small apartments built just for one person. I'm actually a perfect example. I grew up with my family in an old apartment in Daejeon, but three years ago, when I got my job, I moved into a one-bedroom place near my office in Seoul. Another huge change is technology. My parents' apartment still has an old key lock and a heater that makes weird noises, while mine has a digital door lock, and I can even turn on the heating from my phone on the way home. That said, it's kind of a double-edged sword. Homes are way more comfortable now, but prices have skyrocketed, and honestly, buying a place in Seoul feels almost impossible for people my age. So yeah, that's how I think housing has changed in Korea.

questions.en: How has the movie industry changed over the years? How is the way people watch movies today different from the past, and what do you think about these changes?
questions.ko: 영화 산업은 그동안 어떻게 변했나요? 오늘날 사람들이 영화를 보는 방식은 과거와 어떻게 다르며, 이런 변화에 대해 어떻게 생각하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a really interesting question.' → 전체 변화 한 줄 → 차이 2개(극장·DVD → 넷플릭스 같은 스트리밍 / 티켓값 상승으로 극장은 대작 위주) → 내 예시(금요일 밤 집에서 넷플릭스, 큰 액션 영화만 극장) → 내 생각·결론
질문 끝의 'what do you think'를 놓치지 마세요. 좋은 점과 아쉬운 점을 하나씩 말한 뒤 결론을 내리면 됩니다.
AL은 'binge-watch', 'in the comfort of my own home' 같은 생생한 표현으로 내 영화 습관을 묘사하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a really interesting question. The way people watch movies has changed a lot. In the past, people used to go to the theater or rent DVDs. These days, most people watch movies at home on Netflix. For example, in my case, I watch movies at home every Friday night. It's cheap and comfortable. But I still go to the theater for big action movies. I think it's a good change. Yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think the movie industry has changed a lot. In the past, people used to go to the theater or rent DVDs to watch a movie. These days, most people watch movies on streaming services like Netflix. I'd say the biggest reason is convenience. You can watch anything, anytime, on your phone or TV. For example, in my case, every Friday night I watch comedy or action movies on Netflix at home. I'm usually tired after a long week at work, so I love relaxing on my sofa. On the other hand, theater tickets are much more expensive now, so I only go to the theater for big action movies with my friends. Overall, I think it's a good change, but I hope theaters don't disappear. So yeah, that's what I think about the changes.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think the movie industry has gone through a huge transformation over the past ten or twenty years. Back when I was a kid, if you wanted to see a movie, you either went to the theater or rented a DVD from the shop down the street. These days, though, streaming services like Netflix have pretty much taken over, and you can watch almost any movie, anytime, right on your phone. I'd say that's the biggest difference. For example, in my case, Friday night is my movie night. After a long week of meetings, I just curl up on my sofa and binge-watch comedies or action movies in the comfort of my own home. It's cheap, it's easy, and I don't have to deal with crowds. On the other hand, ticket prices at theaters have gone way up, so these days I only go to the theater for big blockbusters that really need a huge screen and loud sound. Personally, I think it's a double-edged sword. Streaming is incredibly convenient, but I'd hate to see theaters disappear, because that shared experience is something special. So yeah, that's what I think about these changes.

questions.en: How has technology changed the way people listen to music? Compare how people listened to music in the past with how they do it now.
questions.ko: 기술은 사람들이 음악을 듣는 방식을 어떻게 바꿔 놓았나요? 과거에 사람들이 음악을 듣던 방식과 지금의 방식을 비교해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a really interesting question.' → 전체 변화 한 줄 → 차이 2개(CD·MP3 플레이어 → 스트리밍 앱 / 앨범 구매 → 추천 플레이리스트) → 내 예시(출퇴근 지하철에서 무선 이어폰으로 IU) → 결론
과거는 used to buy CDs / download songs, 현재는 stream / playlists / wireless earphones 로 대비시키세요.
IH 이상은 '노래를 너무 쉽게 넘겨서 앨범 전체를 듣지 않게 됐다'처럼 단점도 하나 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a really interesting question. Technology changed music a lot. In the past, people used to buy CDs or use MP3 players. These days, most people use streaming apps on their phones. For example, in my case, I listen to music on the subway every day. I use wireless earphones, and I listen to K-pop and ballads. I really like IU. It's much more convenient than before. Yeah, that's how listening to music has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think technology has completely changed the way people listen to music. In the past, people used to buy CDs or download songs to their MP3 players. I remember my first MP3 player in middle school. I could only put about a hundred songs on it. These days, most people just use streaming apps on their phones, so you can listen to millions of songs for a monthly fee. Another big difference is playlists. The app recommends songs for me, so I find new music easily. For example, in my case, I listen to K-pop and ballads on the subway every day with my wireless earphones. On the other hand, I don't really listen to full albums anymore. I just skip songs. So yeah, that's how technology has changed music.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I'd say technology has totally changed the way we listen to music. Back in the day, people used to buy CDs or download songs one by one to their MP3 players. I still remember saving up my allowance in middle school for a tiny MP3 player that could hold maybe a hundred songs, and I felt like the coolest kid in class. These days, though, pretty much everyone just uses a streaming app. For a small monthly fee, you've got millions of songs right in your pocket. The other big difference is how we discover music. The apps make playlists for you based on what you like, so finding new songs is super easy. For example, in my case, I listen to music every single day on my commute. I pop in my wireless earphones on the subway and play my IU playlist, and it really helps me get in the right mood before a long day at the office. That said, it's a bit of a double-edged sword. Because it's so easy to skip songs, I hardly ever listen to a whole album from start to finish anymore. So yeah, that's how I think technology has changed music.

questions.en: What are some problems or concerns that people have about traveling these days? Why do you think these issues have come up?
questions.ko: 요즘 사람들이 여행에 대해 갖는 문제나 걱정거리는 무엇인가요? 왜 이런 문제들이 생겼다고 생각하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a really interesting question.' → 입장 한 줄(가장 큰 걱정은 비용과 인파) → 이유 2개(항공권·호텔 값 상승 / 유명 관광지의 과잉 관광) → 내 경험(작년 여름 Minji와 오사카 — 비싼 항공권, 도톤보리 인파) → 결론
질문이 '왜 생겼는지'도 묻기 때문에 원인(여행하는 사람이 너무 많아짐, SNS 영향)을 꼭 한 문장 넣으세요.
AL은 '마케팅 일을 하다 보니 SNS가 특정 장소를 유명하게 만드는 걸 안다'처럼 내 직업과 연결하면 설득력이 커집니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think people have two big concerns about travel these days. First, it's very expensive. Flights and hotels cost a lot more now. Second, popular places are too crowded. For example, in my case, I went to Osaka with my coworker Minji last summer. The flight was really expensive, and Dotonbori was full of people. I think many people travel now, so these problems came up. Yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think people have two main concerns about traveling these days. First of all, travel has become really expensive. Flight tickets and hotel prices have gone up a lot, especially during summer vacation. On top of that, popular places are way too crowded. I think it's because so many people want to travel again, and everyone sees the same places on social media. For example, in my case, I went to Osaka with my coworker Minji last summer. Our flight tickets were almost twice as expensive as I expected. And when we went to Dotonbori, it was so crowded that we could hardly walk. It was still fun, but it was a little stressful. So next time, I want to go somewhere less famous. So yeah, that's what I think about travel problems these days.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a really interesting question. In my opinion, there are two big concerns people have about traveling these days. First of all, it's just gotten so expensive. Flights, hotels and even food at tourist spots cost way more than they did a few years ago, especially during peak seasons like summer vacation. On top of that, a lot of popular destinations are completely overcrowded. I think part of the reason is that everyone wanted to make up for lost time after the pandemic, and also, social media makes the same few places go viral. Since I work in marketing, I see this all the time. One photo spot gets popular on Instagram, and suddenly thousands of people want to go there. For example, in my case, my coworker Minji and I went to Osaka last summer. Our plane tickets were almost double what I'd expected, and when we got to Dotonbori, it was so packed that we could barely move or take a decent photo. Don't get me wrong, we still had a blast, but it was pretty exhausting. At the end of the day, I think it comes down to planning ahead and choosing less famous places. So yeah, that's what I think about travel issues these days.

questions.en: Some people prefer working from home, while others prefer working at the office. What are the advantages and disadvantages of each? Which do you prefer, and why?
questions.ko: 어떤 사람들은 재택근무를 선호하고, 어떤 사람들은 사무실 근무를 선호합니다. 각각의 장단점은 무엇인가요? 당신은 어느 쪽을 선호하며 그 이유는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a really interesting question.' → 입장(둘을 섞는 방식이 가장 좋다) → 각각의 장단점(재택: 출퇴근 없음·편안함 / 외로움·집중 어려움, 사무실: 팀과 소통 / 출퇴근·회의) → 내 경험(금요일 재택, 9층 창가 자리, Minji와 점심) → 결론
장점과 단점을 각각 하나 이상 꼭 말해야 질문에 다 답한 것이 됩니다. The good thing is ~ / The downside is ~ 로 구분하세요.
실제 페르소나(주 1회 금요일 재택)를 근거로 쓰면 '왜 그 방식을 선호하는지'가 자연스럽게 설명됩니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a really interesting question. Both have good points and bad points. Working from home is comfortable, and you don't need to commute. But it can be lonely. Working at the office is good for talking with your team. But you have to take a crowded subway. For example, in my case, I work from home on Fridays. I like it, but I also like having lunch with my coworkers. So I prefer a mix of both. Yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think both have clear advantages and disadvantages. The good thing about working from home is that you don't have to commute, and you can work in comfortable clothes. The downside is that it can be lonely, and it's easy to get distracted. On the other hand, working at the office is great for teamwork. You can ask questions right away and share ideas. But you have to take crowded subways, and there are a lot of meetings. For example, in my case, I work from home every Friday. I can sleep in a little and focus on writing reports. But from Monday to Thursday, I go to the office, and I really enjoy having lunch with my coworker Minji. So I prefer a mix of both. So yeah, that's what I think about working from home.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a really interesting question. Honestly, I think both options have pretty clear pros and cons. The biggest advantage of working from home is that you don't have to commute, so you save time and energy, and you can work in your pajamas if you want. The downside, though, is that it can get pretty lonely, and it's really easy to get distracted by the bed or the TV. Working at the office, on the other hand, is great for teamwork. When I'm stuck on a marketing campaign, I can just turn around and ask a coworker, and we come up with ideas way faster in person. But of course, there's the packed subway and back-to-back meetings that eat up the whole day. In my case, I actually get the best of both worlds. My company lets us work from home every Friday, so I can sleep in a bit, make a nice cup of coffee and focus on my reports without any interruptions. Then from Monday to Thursday, I'm at my window seat on the ninth floor, chatting with my coworker Minji over lunch. At the end of the day, I think it comes down to balance, so I'd definitely choose a mix of both. So yeah, that's what I think about remote work.

questions.en: Compare living in a big city with living in a small town. Which do you think is better for young people, and why?
questions.ko: 대도시에 사는 것과 작은 마을에 사는 것을 비교해 주세요. 젊은 사람들에게는 어느 쪽이 더 좋다고 생각하며, 그 이유는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, that's a really interesting question.' → 입장(젊은 사람에겐 대도시) → 이유 2개(일자리·커리어 기회 / 교통·편의 시설·문화생활) → 내 경험(대전에서 서울로 와서 IT 회사 취업, 지하철역 5분, 한강) → 반대 측면(집값·스트레스) → 결론
비교 질문이므로 small town 의 장점(조용함, 저렴한 생활비, 여유)도 한두 문장 꼭 언급하세요.
AL은 'Maybe when I'm older, I'd like to ~'처럼 미래 계획을 덧붙여 깊이 있는 결론을 만드세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a really interesting question. Big cities and small towns are very different. Small towns are quiet, and living costs are cheaper. Big cities are busy, but there are more jobs. I think big cities are better for young people. For example, in my case, I moved from Daejeon to Seoul for my job. There are a lot of cafes, restaurants and things to do here. But rent is really expensive. Yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a really interesting question. Living in a big city and living in a small town are very different. Small towns are usually quiet and peaceful, and the cost of living is much lower. But there aren't many jobs or things to do. Big cities are noisy and busy, but they have a lot more opportunities. I think big cities are better for young people, and there are two main reasons. First, there are many more jobs. Second, everything is convenient. For example, in my case, I grew up in Daejeon, but I moved to Seoul three years ago to work at an IT company. My apartment is five minutes from the subway, and I can ride my bike to the Han River. On the other hand, rent is really expensive, and life is stressful. So yeah, that's what I think about city life.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a really interesting question. I think big cities and small towns each have their own appeal. Small towns are usually calm and peaceful, people know their neighbors, and the cost of living is much lower. The catch is that there often aren't many jobs, and there's not a lot to do on weekends. Big cities, on the other hand, are noisy and crowded, but they're full of opportunities. Personally, I think big cities are better for young people, for two main reasons. First of all, that's where the jobs are, especially in fields like IT and marketing. On top of that, city life is just incredibly convenient. For example, in my case, I grew up in Daejeon, which is a lot quieter than Seoul, and three years ago I moved here for my job. Now there's a subway station five minutes from my apartment, cafes on every corner, and I can bike to the Han River in ten minutes. That said, it's not all perfect. My rent eats up a big chunk of my salary, and the pace of life can be really stressful. Maybe when I'm older, I'd like to move somewhere quieter. But for now, the city is where I want to be. So yeah, that's what I think about city life.

pronunciation.tip: '스펜'에 강세. 끝 v는 윗니를 아랫입술에 대고
